## Completed line: Tame

`line/Tame` proves the unchanged theorem `Tame : H01Statement ∧ H02Statement`.
H01 includes exponential-sequence smoothing and all six frozen calculus
clauses. H02 constructs genuine inverse-family derivatives from the resolvent
identity and proves the required local tame bounds. Ordered-partition
composition and multilinear normalization supply the higher-order estimates,
including order zero and seminorms with nontrivial kernels.

All 15 new proof modules are in the root import. At proof commit
`4e255f2dfff527c143babbdd491762dd8ec8d092`, the default build passed all 3,810 jobs,
the project axiom audit passed, and `#print axioms ContinuousFlexibility.Blueprint.Tame`
reported only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
[Verified build](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/continuous-flexibility/actions/runs/42982787838).
No frozen statement or assembly repair was needed.

The [PR integration build](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/continuous-flexibility/actions/runs/42982795292)
also passed with main's completed N12 proof: 3,814 jobs, an axiom audit of
11,066 project declarations (8,324 theorems), and 9 / 42 blueprint statements proved.

## Target

`thm:main` of the manuscript. The statement was first taken from the 62-page version
(`paper/flexible-surface-rewrite/01-introduction.tex`, lines 18–31); the 104-page readable version
(`paper/flexible-surface-readable/`) has the same theorems, constants and labels with more of the
proofs written out, and is the version the task files cite:
a smooth, one-periodic family of isometric embeddings of the standard sphere with two
noncongruent images, fixed inner disk and cap, and constant area, enclosed volume and
total mean curvature.

The manuscript contains no author-flagged unproved step. It treats the oscillator and Morse
spectra and Hamilton's Nash–Moser theorem as standard inputs; none of these is in mathlib.

### R06a: correction of the local test class (line/R06a, 2026-11-11)

The frozen clause
`∀ u d, (u, d) ∈ TailFormLift T endCut → TailWeakDerivative T endCut u d`
used the test condition `Function.support ψ ⊆ Ioo T.entrance endCut`.
Together with `HasCompactSupport ψ` this does **not** say that the support is
compactly contained in the open interval: its closure may meet the singular
endpoint. The resulting weak-derivative clause is false for the allowed weights.

Here is the counterexample mechanism, including why the deep-tail inequalities
do not prevent it. Choose mass and gap intervals of length `l_n ≍ ε 2^(-n)`,
with density `1/l_n` on each mass interval and a plateau of height
`g_n = exp(-4 n^4)` on most of each gap. Smooth the transitions in arbitrarily
short collars. Then the mass intervals have mass `1` and resistance `l_n^2`;
the gaps have mass at most `2 g_n l_n` and resistance between
`l_n/(2 g_n)` and `2 l_n/g_n`. Starting sufficiently far out and taking ε
small makes the smallness conditions arbitrarily small and the two mass times
resistance conditions arbitrarily large. The density is smooth and positive
at every interior point, as required.

In the plateau of gap n place a smooth bump `u_n` of height `exp(n^4)`, and a
smooth cutoff `ψ_n` of height `exp(-n^4)` which is constant on the support of
`u_n`. The disjoint sums `u = Σ u_n`, `d = Σ u_n'` have finite weighted energy;
their finite partial sums prove `(u,d)` is in the stated form closure. The sum
`ψ = Σ ψ_n` extends smoothly and flatly across the endpoint and has ordinary
support in the open interval. However, `u ψ' = 0`, whereas
`∫ |d ψ| = ∞`, since every gap contributes the same positive variation.
Adding the compactly supported test `q = u_m'` for one fixed gap gives
`∫ u (ψ+q)' = -∫ (u_m')^2 < 0`, while `d (ψ+q)` is still nonintegrable.
Lean's total integral of that nonintegrable function is zero. Thus this is
an actual failure of the frozen equality, not just a missing integrability lemma.

The local tests and the Friedrichs core now require
`tsupport ψ ⊆ Ioo T.entrance endCut`. The same corrected definitions feed
`R06Operator`, `R06Full`, `R06Statement`, and `R06_of_nodes`; no inverse or
convergence conclusion has been removed. The complete proof is
assembled in `Radial.TailDeepInverse` and `Blueprint.R06a`, using actual weighted
mass averages, smooth resistance hats, a reflected coercive form, and the
positive-resolvent identity for truncations. Its constants are `C = 4`,
`η₀ = 1/10`, and `K₀ = 10 * tailSmoothStepConstant + 2`. The independent scalar
operator definitions have moved unchanged to `Statements.DeepTailOperator` to
keep this proof layer independent of the oscillator and physical reference data.
R06a is closed. [CI run 42986219745](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/continuous-flexibility/actions/runs/42986219745)
passed all default targets, including `AxiomAudit`, and printed

No sub-blueprint or additional analytic hypothesis was needed.

### N04: actual physical pieces and boundary inverses (line/N04b and line/N04Coordinates, 2026-11-11)

The old domain clause in `Statements/Nonlinear.lean` was

```lean
def physicalPieceOpen (S : PhysicalSpacesData) (K : CanonicalData S) (m : ℕ) : Set PolarPoint :=
  Ioo (K.physicalLeft m) (K.physicalRight m) ×ˢ univ
```

For every state, the chart and inverse were required to map between this same
physical rectangle and `canonicalOpen S K m`. The paired halves shared the fixed
radius `K.physicalRight (K.cutPair m).1 = K.physicalLeft (K.cutPair m).2`.
The readable manuscript instead splits a negative component at the travel level
`σ = T/2` (`eq:fixed-strip-coordinates`, `eq:fixed-strip-cut`): its physical
preimage is an inverse-chart curve, allowed to depend on the state and angle.
The actual characteristic and return equations do not identify that curve with
a state-independent physical radius. The old rectangle clause therefore does
not express the manuscript construction without an additional, unproved
identification. This records an unusable domain encoding for that construction;
it does **not** assert a formalized negation of the entire old `N04bStatement`.

The repaired `CanonicalData` has
`physicalDomain : (AnnularState S × ℝ) → ℕ → Set PolarPoint`, and
`physicalPieceOpen S K z m = K.physicalDomain z m`. The old rectangle remains
`referencePhysicalPieceOpen`; the reference state and positive pieces retain
it. `CanonicalGeometry` requires actual open, periodic, reflection-invariant
domains, the appropriate sign, and unique coverage outside a planar null set.
`CanonicalCurrentCutPair` requires the two negative domains to be disjoint and
cover their component off the common curve
`θ ↦ K.inverseChart z (K.cutPair m).1 (K.cutRadius m, θ)`, with the same curve
from the right inverse and the correct two root-circle images.

The old boundary clause prescribed smooth chart and height values, nonzero
Jacobian and positive height on the radial closed rectangle, but specified the
stored inverse identities only on open sets. The repaired boundary clause uses
`closure (physicalPieceOpen S K z m)` and `canonicalClosed S K m`, includes
both closed inverse identities and both closed mapping properties, and requires
the stored inverse to agree on a full neighborhood with a genuine smooth local
inverse at every boundary point (`CanonicalBoundaryInverseGerm`). Thus the
ordinary boundary derivatives in the transmission equation refer to that
inverse. Normalization retains chart/height equality and also fixes the actual
domains on the normalization region; source pairing integrates over the actual
physical piece.

`N04PartA` and `N04PartB` now use the shared `CanonicalGeometry` and
`CanonicalCutOperatorProperties` predicates. `N04Properties` combines these with
the unchanged all-order quantitative clause and actual source pairing;
`Blueprint/Assembly.lean:N04_of_nodes` passes these four parts to the same final
target. The existential forms of `N04aStatement`, `N04bStatement` and
`N04cStatement`, and the parent signature
`N04Coordinates (hN04b : N04bStatement) : N04cStatement`, are unchanged. In
particular, one neighborhood and one loss still precede every derivative order,
the material bound is still uniform in the state and component, and the exact
canonical operator, transmission and cubic-division conclusions are retained.
This is an explicit repair of the geometric predicates, not a replacement of
the all-order target by a conditional or finite-order result.

# N04Coordinates-Realization

## Problem

Prove `ContinuousFlexibility.Blueprint.N04CoordinatesRealization` in
`src/ContinuousFlexibility/Blueprint/N04Coordinates/Realization.lean`:

```lean
theorem N04CoordinatesRealization
    (hFlowJets : N04FlowJetsTarget) (hN04b : N04bStatement) : N04cStatement
```

The flow-tool input is the independent raw-field ODE theorem in
`src/ContinuousFlexibility/Analysis/N04FlowJetsTarget.lean`.
Construct a legitimately controlled correction and canonical-coordinate
witness, while retaining the cumulative N01–N03 conditions, and derive
the exact all-order potential and divided-coefficient bound on one
common state neighborhood with one fixed loss.

The same witness must also carry both `CanonicalPrimitiveGeometry` and
`CanonicalGeometry.PrimitiveGeometryProperties` from the current parent
statement. The latter retains the actual radial reference gauge, reference
principal positivity and unit-piece jets, current-minus-reference spatial
jets and their `SmoothDirections` tower with the prescribed height gain,
the radial supported auxiliary source, and `TransmissionGeometry`.
In particular, relative transport matching alone does not replace the
actual forward chart and height first-jet matching at roots and at the
state-dependent middle cuts. See `docs/notes/N07a-interface-repair.md`.

The proof includes the actual root charts and heights, global negative
pieces and cut matching, positive reference interpolation and finite
boundary jets, inverse coordinates, ordinary boundary jets, and the
actual three vanishing numerator jets at both ends. Quantitative
constants must have the exact quantifier order in N04Properties.
The source-pairing identity is already available from N04PartA.

An arbitrary PartA/B witness is not assumed to have the required bounds.
If a witness is replaced or its neighborhood shrunk, every retained
N01–N03 and canonical clause must be proved for that same replacement.
Per-state or per-component positive collars do not by themselves give
the required common state neighborhood. No final canonical estimate may
be inserted as a new hypothesis.

## Completion standard

- The theorem has exactly the statement above and contains no `sorry`.
- Its axiom audit contains only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
- Every used module compiles and the complete CI is green.
- The exact parent `N04Coordinates` must assemble this theorem and
  `N04CoordinatesFlowJets` without a local `sorry`; it is complete only
  after both dependencies also have the permitted axiom set.

/-!
# Preserving the cumulative construction on a smaller neighborhood

Every coordinate smallness argument may increase the base order and decrease
the radius. The earlier nonlinear properties, including their genuine
directional derivative towers and fixed-loss estimates, then hold on that
same new neighborhood. No data are replaced in this restriction step.
-/

private theorem restrict_directional_bound
    {E : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    {U V : Set E} {f : E → ℝ} {p : ℕ → Seminorm ℝ E}
    (hV : IsOpen V) (hsub : V ⊆ U) (hp : Monotone p)
    {base base' high high' : ℕ} (hb : base ≤ base') (hh : high ≤ high')
    (x0 : E) (k : ℕ) {A w : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A)
    (h : ∃ J : SmoothDirections U f, ∀ z ∈ U, ∀ v : Fin k → E,
      w * |J.D k z v| ≤ A * oneHighVariationWeight p base high (z - x0) v) :
    ∃ J : SmoothDirections V f, ∀ z ∈ V, ∀ v : Fin k → E,
      w * |J.D k z v| ≤ A * oneHighVariationWeight p base' high' (z - x0) v := by
  obtain ⟨J, hJ⟩ := h
  refine ⟨smoothDirectionsRestrict J hV hsub, fun z hz v => ?_⟩
  exact (hJ z (hsub hz) v).trans
    (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (oneHighVariationWeight_mono hp hb hh _ v) hA)

private theorem n01CoefficientJetBounds_restrict
    {D : ReferenceData} {T : MaterialData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {base base' loss loss' : ℕ} {ε ε' : ℝ}
    (hD : IsAccumulatingProfile D) (hT : IsMaterialData D T)
    (h : N01CoefficientJetBounds D T S C base loss ε)
    (hb : base ≤ base') (hl : loss ≤ loss') (hε : ε' ≤ ε) :
    N01CoefficientJetBounds D T S C base' loss' ε' := by
  intro k s
  obtain ⟨B, hB, hbound⟩ := h k s
  refine ⟨B, hB, ?_⟩
  intro m i a b p hab hp
  have hgrade : Monotone (pairGrading (stateGrading S) realGrading) :=
    tamePairGrading_monotone (stateGrading_monotone S) (fun _ _ _ => le_rfl)
  simpa only [one_mul] using restrict_directional_bound
    (isOpen_stateNeighborhood S C base' ε') (stateNeighborhood_mono S C hb hε)
    hgrade hb (Nat.add_le_add_left hl s) (C.referenceState, 0) k
    (w := 1) (materialSample_factor_nonneg hD hT hB.le m)
    (by simpa only [one_mul] using hbound m i a b p hab hp)

private theorem n01FlowJetBounds_restrict
    {D : ReferenceData} {T : MaterialData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {base base' loss loss' : ℕ} {ε ε' : ℝ}
    (hD : IsAccumulatingProfile D) (hT : IsMaterialData D T)
    (h : N01FlowJetBounds T S C base loss ε)
    (hb : base ≤ base') (hl : loss ≤ loss') (hε : ε' ≤ ε) :
    N01FlowJetBounds T S C base' loss' ε' := by
  intro k s
  obtain ⟨B, hB, hbound⟩ := h k s
  refine ⟨B, hB, ?_⟩
  intro m a b p hab hp
  have hgrade : Monotone (pairGrading (stateGrading S) realGrading) :=
    tamePairGrading_monotone (stateGrading_monotone S) (fun _ _ _ => le_rfl)
  exact restrict_directional_bound (isOpen_stateNeighborhood S C base' ε')

/-!
# A residual-preserving bound for the actual N03 error

The source error is bilinear in a circle residual and a height test.
Its smooth tame clause therefore gives a homogeneous estimate in these
two different spaces. The neighborhood and loss below are chosen once,
before the output order, residual and test; no constant independent of
the residual is added.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace ContinuousFlexibility.Analysis

open Set
open ContinuousFlexibility.Statements

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

/-- Remove the zero base point in abstract spaces, before instantiating
the concrete projective sector. All spaces and gradings are fixed
explicitly when applying the heterogeneous estimate. -/
private theorem heterogeneousBilinear_tame_bounds_at_zero
    {Z E F G : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace Z] [AddCommGroup Z] [Module ℝ Z]
    [TopologicalSpace E] [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace F] [AddCommGroup F] [Module ℝ F]
    [TopologicalSpace G] [AddCommGroup G] [Module ℝ G] [T2Space G]
    {a : ℕ → Seminorm ℝ Z} {p : ℕ → Seminorm ℝ E}
    {q : ℕ → Seminorm ℝ F} {r : ℕ → Seminorm ℝ G}
    {U : Set Z} {A : Z → E →ₗ[ℝ] F →ₗ[ℝ] G}
    (hT : SmoothTameOn (pairGrading (pairGrading a p) q) r ((U ×ˢ univ) ×ˢ univ)
      (fun z : (Z × E) × F => A z.1.1 z.1.2 z.2))
    (hz : (0 : Z) ∈ U) :
    ∃ loss low : ℕ, ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧
      ∀ s : ℕ, low ≤ s → ∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧
        ∀ z ∈ U, a low z < δ → ∀ e : E, ∀ f : F,
          r s (A z e f) ≤ B *
            ((1 + a (s + loss) z) * (p low e * q low f) +
              (p (s + loss) e * q low f + p low e * q (s + loss) f)) := by
  obtain ⟨loss, low, δ, hδ, hb⟩ :=
    heterogeneousBilinear_tame_bounds_on_ball_of_smoothTame
      (Z := Z) (E := E) (F := F) (G := G)
      (a := a) (p := p) (q := q) (r := r) (U := U) (A := A) (z₀ := 0) hT hz
  refine ⟨loss, low, δ, hδ, ?_⟩
  intro s hs
  obtain ⟨B, hB, hb⟩ := hb s hs
  refine ⟨B, hB, ?_⟩
  intro z hz hlow e f
  exact hb z hz (by simpa only [sub_zero] using hlow) e f

private theorem seminorm_pair_zero_lt
    {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    (p : Seminorm ℝ E) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    p 0 < ε ∧ |(0 : ℝ)| < ε := by
  simpa only [map_zero, abs_zero] using And.intro hε hε

/-- The N03 smooth tame error has one common low neighborhood and loss,
with one high factor among the sector parameter, residual and test. -/
theorem n03Error_homogeneous_tame_bound
    {D : ReferenceData} {T : MaterialData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {R : ReturnEquationData S}
    {L : ReturnCorrectionData S} {base : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hN03 : N03Properties D T S C R L base ε) :
    ∃ loss low : ℕ, ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧
      ∀ s : ℕ, low ≤ s → ∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧
        ∀ v ∈ sectorNeighborhood S base ε ε,
          pairGrading (sectorGrading S) realGrading low v < δ →
          ∀ r : CircleSpace S, ∀ η : HeightPair S,
            S.sourceGrading s (L.error (liftSectorParameter S C v) r η) ≤ B *
              ((1 + pairGrading (sectorGrading S) realGrading (s + loss) v) *
                  ((S.circle (3 / 4 : ℝ)).grading low r * heightPairGrading S low η) +
                ((S.circle (3 / 4 : ℝ)).grading (s + loss) r * heightPairGrading S low η +
                  (S.circle (3 / 4 : ℝ)).grading low r *
                    heightPairGrading S (s + loss) η)) := by
  have hSmooth : SmoothTameOn
      (pairGrading (pairGrading (pairGrading (sectorGrading S) realGrading)
        (S.circle (3 / 4 : ℝ)).grading) (heightPairGrading S))
      S.sourceGrading ((sectorNeighborhood S base ε ε ×ˢ univ) ×ˢ univ)
      (fun z : ((StateDirections S × ℝ) × CircleSpace S) × HeightPair S =>
        L.error (liftSectorParameter S C z.1.1) z.1.2 z.2) := hN03.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hz₀ : (0 : StateDirections S × ℝ) ∈ sectorNeighborhood S base ε ε := by
    change sectorGrading S base (0 : StateDirections S) < ε ∧ |(0 : ℝ)| < ε
    exact seminorm_pair_zero_lt (sectorGrading S base) hε
  exact heterogeneousBilinear_tame_bounds_at_zero
    (Z := StateDirections S × ℝ) (E := CircleSpace S) (F := HeightPair S) (G := S.Source)
    (a := pairGrading (sectorGrading S) realGrading)
    (p := (S.circle (3 / 4 : ℝ)).grading) (q := heightPairGrading S) (r := S.sourceGrading)
    (U := sectorNeighborhood S base ε ε)
    (A := fun v : StateDirections S × ℝ => L.error (liftSectorParameter S C v))
    hSmooth hz₀

end ContinuousFlexibility.Analysis
